messages:
Morgan: FYI repro'd a consistent tail-latency blip on long-context runs when FIFO eviction is enabled. ~200-500ms 95p token latency spikes under write-amplification >2.
Ina: repro steps? test harness or prod?
Morgan: happ'd on perf lab with replay workload (repro script attached). short gist: many small writes that partially overlap hot prefixes. FIFO seemed to evict a page still referenced by reuse logic, forcing a costly page-in + rebuild.
Raj: can you paste the small log snippet that shows the eviction + missing-reuse event?
Morgan: sure — here's the relevant snippet and a tiny annotated trace:```
[2025-05-03T14:10:12Z] kv: evict page id=0x7f3a size=256KB policy=FIFO
[2025-05-03T14:10:12Z] kv: reuse check failed key=hdr:chunk:923 reason=paged_out
[2025-05-03T14:10:12Z] runtime: rebuild_kv_page id=0x7f3a cost=12ms
[2025-05-03T14:10:12Z] kernel-selection: fallback to scalar path (quant) added 30ms
[2025-05-03T14:10:12Z] overall-token-latency single_token=320ms
```
Ina: ugh. so eviction wins, then reuse path observes paged_out, triggers synchronous page rebuild on hot path. That explains tail.
Sylvia: did you try LRU in the same harness?
Morgan: yes — same workload with LRU gave much flatter tail (95p ~ 60ms). But LRU throughput suffers a bit when memory pressure is sustained; FIFO had slightly better avg throughput.
Raj: important to know if correctness is involved (i.e., double-free or use-after-evict). logs don't show crashes, just synchronous rebuilds.
Morgan: no OOM/crash, just blocking in refill path. Also noticed fragmentation grows over very long contexts: free lists scatter, so reclaim path sometimes scans multiple arena buckets — adds a few ms.
Ina: any perf profiles? pprof/Flamegraph?
Morgan: attached flame excerpt (inline): ```
Top: rebuild_kv_page -> refill_page -> memcpy -> kernel_dispatch -> quant_path_fallback
rebuild_kv_page  (12ms)
memcpy  (4ms)
kernel_dispatch (18ms fallback penalty included)
```
Raj: kernel selection fallback there is interesting — suggests when page is rebuilt, we pick a different code path (maybe unquantized) because metadata not set. Are we missing metadata persistence on page writeback?
Sylvia: could also be batching heuristics: rebuild_path triggers single-token sync work and bypasses batch coalescing, so you lose batching benefits and kernel selection picks scalar.
Morgan: exactly. observed that if we delay eviction until next batch window (10ms), the rebuild often piggybacks and batching absorbs it. But that increases memory footprint.
Ina: tradeoff: tail latency vs memory. We should consider hybrid policy: FIFO for cold pages, LRU for recently reused pages, or mark-and-scan hot set.
Raj: propose small experiment: 1) add reuse-protect window: when page reused within X ms, promote it (LRU-style). 2) opportunistic async rebuild: schedule rebuild off hot RPC thread so request sees a placeholder that pulls from async work (with fallback).
Sylvia: also add a quick fix: ensure page metadata persists a kernel-hint bit so kernel-selection stays stable after rebuild. If metadata missing, we default to scalar.
Morgan: good plan. I'll sketch a PR for (1) and (3) tonight. For immediate mitigation in prod, we can flip FIFO->LRU on a limited pool.
ci-bot: deploy queued: kv/evict-policy-toggle -> canary env (pool-7). Runbook: revert with /deploy cancel within 15m.
Morgan: thanks. I'll post repro script and pprof links in the thread. Will follow up with microbenchmark numbers after PR. :thumbsup:
